title: Writing Your Own Module: Validation, Dynamic Blocks, and Tests
intro: The earlier module tutorials used modules other people wrote. Now your team has written one, in modules/web_sg: a security group whose ingress rules are generated from a list of ports. A module is an interface: variables are its inputs, outputs are its return values, and everything else is private. This tutorial exercises that interface the way a reviewer would.

steps.prompt: Check the module on its own, without touching any backend or state. First initialise it in its directory, modules/web_sg, with the backend disabled.
steps.fake_output:
Initializing provider plugins...
- Installing hashicorp/aws v5.70.0...

Terraform has been successfully initialized!
steps.explanation: Providers are installed for the module directory, and no state backend was configured.
steps.why: -chdir runs Terraform as if you'd changed into that directory, which keeps CI scripts free of cd. -backend=false is what makes this safe in a pull-request check: it needs no credentials for the state bucket, so it can run on untrusted branches.

steps.prompt: Now validate the module in modules/web_sg.
steps.explanation: The module's syntax, references, and types are consistent.
steps.why: validate checks the module in isolation: every variable it reads is declared, every attribute exists on its resource type. It doesn't call the cloud API, so it can't tell you a VPC id is wrong. That's plan's job. Run fmt, validate, then plan, cheapest first.

steps.prompt: The module declares a validation rule: environment must be dev, staging, or prod. From the root configuration, prove the rule works by planning with environment set to qa.
steps.fake_output:
Error: Invalid value for variable

  on main.tf line 14, in module "web_sg":
  14:   environment = var.environment
    var.environment is "qa"

environment must be dev, staging, or prod.

This was checked by the validation rule at modules/web_sg/variables.tf:9,3-13.
steps.explanation: The plan stopped before reading any infrastructure, with the module author's own message.
steps.why: A validation block turns a mistake into a clear error at plan time, in the caller's terms. Without it, a typo such as 'prd' flows into names and tags, and you find out from a strangely named resource in the console. Validate anything with a small set of legal values: environments, instance sizes, CIDR formats.

steps.prompt: Plan with the real values (the defaults) and see what the module's dynamic block generates from ingress_ports = [80, 443].
steps.explanation: One dynamic block in the module became two ingress blocks, one per port.
steps.why: for_each and count repeat whole resources. A dynamic block repeats a nested block inside one resource (ingress rules, disk attachments, tags on some resources), which nothing else can do. Use it only for that: a dynamic block is harder to read than literal blocks, so two fixed rules should stay written out.

steps.prompt: The module has tests in its tests/ directory (.tftest.hcl files). Run them from modules/web_sg.
steps.fake_output:
tests/ports.tftest.hcl... in progress
  run "creates_one_rule_per_port"... pass
  run "rejects_unknown_environment"... pass
tests/ports.tftest.hcl... tearing down
tests/ports.tftest.hcl... pass

Success! 2 passed, 0 failed.
steps.explanation: Both test runs passed: the rule count matches the port list, and a bad environment is rejected.
steps.why: terraform test (built in since 1.6) runs plan or apply against the module and checks assertions. With 'command = plan' and mocked providers, it needs no cloud account and runs in seconds. Tests are what let you change a shared module without breaking the twenty configurations that call it.

steps.prompt: Apply has run. Read the module's result the way a caller would: show the root output web_sg_id.
steps.explanation: The security group's id, passed up from the module's own output.
steps.why: A caller can only see what a module declares as outputs; its resources are otherwise private. So outputs are a contract: removing or renaming one breaks callers, like changing a function's return value. Publish modules with a version tag and pin callers to it (terraform-tutorial-008), so a change reaches each environment when that team chooses.
